note: Provenance and payload record for every file this repository vendors into internal/web/static/vendor. A vendored file in a public repository is a file this project answers for, so the package, the exact version, the URL it was fetched from, its SHA-256, its byte size and its licence are recorded as data rather than claimed in a comment. To re-vendor a file: fetch the new url, replace the file, and update sha256 and bytes here in the same commit -- internal/web/static_vendor_test.go walks this file and the tree in both directions and fails if either side is missing an entry. The payload budget is not stored here on purpose: a budget a contributor can raise by editing the file it is checked against is not a budget. It lives in that test as a constant.

files.url_note: The lit npm package ships no single-file bundle; github.com/lit/dist is the Lit team's own prebuilt distribution repository and v3.3.3 is its tag for this release. The raw URL at the tag is used rather than a CDN's semver-resolving alias so the URL is immutable.
The package's own `exports.import` entry point. It is minified and self-contained: it bundles a copy of @dagrejs/graphlib and re-exports it as `graphlib`.
The version @dagrejs/dagre 3.1.1 depends on, vendored standalone so the layout code builds its graphs against a module it imports by name instead of reaching through dagre's re-export.
